questions.question: What is the MITRE ATT&CK framework in the context of Security Incident Response?

options.text: A knowledge base of common tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTP) for threat modeling

explanation.correct: The MITRE-ATT&CK framework is a knowledge base of common tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTP) that organizations can access to develop specific threat models and methodologies against cyberattacks.

wrongAnswers.explanation: MITRE ATT&CK is a knowledge base, not a vulnerability scanner
MITRE ATT&CK describes adversary behavior, not firewall configurations
MITRE ATT&CK is for threat intelligence, not compliance reporting

source.excerpt: The MITRE-ATT&CK framework is a knowledge base of common tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTP) that your organization can access to develop specific threat models and methodologies against cyberattacks.

labels.domain: Security Incident Response Overview and Data Visualization

questions.question: Which three MITRE ATT&CK matrices are used to describe adversary behaviors? (Choose three.)

explanation.correct: ATT&CK consists of three matrices: Enterprise ATT&CK (enterprise network and cloud), ICS ATT&CK (Industrial Control Systems), and Mobile ATT&CK (mobile devices).

wrongAnswers.explanation: Cloud is covered within Enterprise ATT&CK, not as a separate matrix
Database ATT&CK is not a standard MITRE matrix

source.excerpt: ATT&CK consists of the following matrices: Enterprise ATT&CK, ICS ATT&CK, Mobile ATT&CK

labels.domain: Security Incident Response Overview and Data Visualization

questions.question: What represents 'the why' of an ATT&CK technique?

explanation.correct: Tactics represent the 'why' of an ATT&CK technique. It is the adversary's tactical objective for performing an action. Techniques represent 'how' an adversary achieves a tactical objective.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Procedures are specific implementations of techniques
Techniques represent 'how' an adversary achieves an objective, not 'why'
A matrix is the organizational structure, not the 'why'

source.excerpt: Tactics represent the why of an ATT&CK technique. It is the adversary's tactical objective for performing an action.

labels.domain: Security Incident Response Overview and Data Visualization

questions.question: What is an intent-based response in Security Incident Response?

options.text: A response based on user intentions
A dynamic kill chain framework to correlate incidents and predict adversary behavior

explanation.correct: An intent-based response uses a dynamic and contextual kill chain framework that can help correlate security incidents and identify a large scope of attacks. It enables predicting attacker behavior so resources can be focused effectively.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Intent-based refers to adversary intent, not user intentions
Intent-based response is about predicting attacker behavior, not compliance
Intent-based response enables automated prediction, not manual workflows

source.excerpt: An intent-based response uses a dynamic and contextual kill chain framework that can help your organization to correlate security incidents and to identify a large scope of attacks.

labels.domain: Security Incident Response Overview and Data Visualization

questions.question: Which roles are required to access the Security Incident Response Explorer dashboard? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: The roles required to access the Security Incident Response Explorer dashboard are: sn_si.admin (to write) and sn_si_basic (to read).

wrongAnswers.explanation: itil is an ITSM role, not specific to SIR
admin is a general role; specific SIR roles are required

source.excerpt: Roles required: sn_si.admin (to write), sn_si_basic (to read)

labels.domain: Security Incident Response Overview and Data Visualization

questions.question:
Which statements about MITRE ATT&CK integration with Security Operations are true?
a) SIEM integrations ingest threat data with relevant TTPs associated to security incidents
b) When an IoC is associated to a security incident, Threat Intelligence automatically searches threat feeds
c) MITRE ATT&CK cannot be integrated with Vulnerability Response
d) CVE context information is shared for each technique

explanation.correct: Statements a, b, and d are true. SIEM integrations associate TTPs, TI searches threat feeds for IoCs, and CVE context is shared. Statement c is false - MITRE ATT&CK CAN be integrated with Vulnerability Response to determine if business-critical assets are threatened.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Statement c is false - ATT&CK integrates with VR
Statements b and d are also true
Statement a is also true

source.excerpt: MITRE-ATT&CK also shares CVE context information for each technique. Your security team can review the exploited techniques in Vulnerability Response.

labels.domain: Security Incident Response Overview and Data Visualization

questions.question: Which path is used to access the Security Incident Response Explorer dashboard?

explanation.correct: To access the Security Incident Response Explorer, navigate to All > Self-Service > Homepage or navigate to Self-Service > Dashboards, then choose Security Incident Explorer from the reports list.

wrongAnswers.explanation: This path doesn't lead to the Explorer dashboard
Reports path is incorrect; use Self-Service
This is for Vulnerability Response, not SIR

source.excerpt: Navigate to All > Self-Service > Homepage or navigate to Self-Service > Dashboards. Choose Security Incident Explorer from the reports list.

labels.domain: Security Incident Response Overview and Data Visualization

questions.question: How can techniques be associated with tactics in MITRE ATT&CK?

options.text: Each technique belongs to exactly one tactic
Techniques may be associated with more than one tactic
Tactics and techniques are never associated
Only sub-techniques can span multiple tactics

explanation.correct: Techniques may be associated with more than one tactic. For example, Access Token Manipulation is used by an adversary to achieve either the tactic of Privilege Escalation or Defense Evasion.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Techniques can span multiple tactics
Tactics and techniques are directly related in the ATT&CK framework
Both techniques and sub-techniques can span multiple tactics

source.excerpt: Techniques may be associated with more than one tactic. For example, Access Token Manipulation is used by an adversary to achieve either the tactic of Privilege Escalation or Defense Evasion.

labels.domain: Security Incident Response Overview and Data Visualization

questions.question: How can organizations benefit from using MITRE ATT&CK in Security Operations? (Choose two.)

options.text: Equip analysts with TTPs to better analyze and respond to incidents
Automate incident workflows using playbooks in ATT&CK context
Eliminate the need for vulnerability scanning

explanation.correct: Organizations benefit by equipping security analysts with MITRE-ATT&CK TTPs to better analyze and respond to incidents, and by automating incident workflows using playbooks in the context of the MITRE-ATT&CK framework.

wrongAnswers.explanation: ATT&CK enhances security tools, it doesn't replace them
ATT&CK complements vulnerability scanning, doesn't eliminate it

source.excerpt: Equip security analysts with MITRE-ATT&CK tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) to better analyze and respond to security incidents. Automate the incident workflows using the playbook for detecting and containing threats in the context of the MITRE-ATT&CK framework.

labels.domain: Security Incident Response Overview and Data Visualization

questions.question: Which applications are categorized under Enterprise Security Case Management in Security Operations? (Choose three.)

explanation.correct: Enterprise security case management applications include Security Incident Response, Major Security Incident Management, Data Loss Prevention Incident Response, Threat Intelligence, and TISC. These help respond to critical incidents.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Security Posture Control falls under USEM (Unified Security Exposure Management), not case management.
Vulnerability Response is part of USEM, not enterprise security case management.

source.excerpt: Enterprise security case management applications: Security Incident Response, Major Security Incident Management, Data Loss Prevention Incident Response, Threat Intelligence, Threat Intelligence Security Center (TISC).

labels.domain: Security Incident Response Overview and Data Visualization

questions.question: What happens when an analyst selects a donut chart item in the Security Incident Overview section?

options.text: A report is generated and emailed
It navigates to the respective record with a filtered list view
The chart expands to show more details
A new security incident is created

explanation.correct: The donut charts in the Overview section are drill-down enabled. When an analyst selects any chart item, it navigates to the respective record with a filtered list view of items within that corresponding tab.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Reports are not automatically emailed when clicking chart items.
The interaction navigates to filtered records rather than expanding the chart.
Clicking chart items filters existing data, not creates new incidents.

source.excerpt: The donut charts are drill down enabled, when an analyst selects any of the chart items, then it navigates you to the respective record with a filtered list view.

labels.domain: Security Incident Response Overview and Data Visualization
